adjudication.rationale: Dense-hit cells (>100 matches on one page) nondeterministically lose early-yielded hits: the search stream's AsyncStream bufferingNewest(100) policy evicts the oldest buffered results when the consumer lags a burst (measured host: scan-sim run-1 v01 dropped 11 of 141 page-5 hits while run-2 and the vector twin kept all; final-cache re-derivation confirms 141 is the true count). Freeze takes the higher-yield run per cell (drops only lose hits); the drop mechanism is F12-08. Applies mechanically to any burst cell the freeze phase reconciles, not only r06.

'(a+)+b' is the canonical ReDoS shape; rejection (empty stream) is the ratified sentinel/precheck design working as intended. The oracle's pure-regex matches ('ab' substrings inside ordinary words) are unreachable by design. No finding.
